Paragraph: Those who are interested in self-realization, in terms of mind and sense control, offer the functions of all the senses, as well as the vital force [breath], as oblations into the fire of the controlled mind.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Restlessness of the mind and body driven by automatic sensory impulses and unregulated vital energies.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states: 'Those who are interested in self-realization, in terms of mind and sense control, offer the functions of all the senses, as well as the vital force [breath], as oblations into the fire of the controlled mind.'
Outcome/Resolution: Subduing sensory functions and breath under the authority of a illumination-seeking mind yields deep inner tranquility.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Somatic Regulation: Harmonizing breath and physiological functions to achieve psychological balance
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Cognitive Mastery: Directing mental attention intentionally rather than reacting automatically
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Inner Stillness: Quieting physical and mental commotion to experience internal peace

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Sarvanindriya-karmani prana-karmani capare (Offering all sensory and vital breath functions)
Atma-samyama-yogagnau juhvati (Sacrificing into the fire of self-restraint and mental control)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Yogis achieve self-realization by merging all sensory actions and vital breaths into the ignited fire of mental discipline.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Regulating physiological responses and breath restores emotional balance and halts compulsive reactive behavior.
